title: PulseCare POC scoping - quality eval plan

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-02 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 mins | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood); Maya Ortiz, Dr. Ravi Patel, Sam Lee, Jordan (PulseCare)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on POC quality evaluation plan, define golden prompts, regression test plan, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, and timeline.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood here, AE on this one. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya Ortiz: Hey Alex, Maya here.
[00:10] Ravi Patel: Ravi here.
[00:12] Sam Lee: Sam, Platform.
[00:14] Jordan: Jordan from procurement.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Priya, SE at Redwood. I'll lead the eval plan details.

[00:45] Alex Chen: High level, PulseCare wants to validate model quality and safety for clinical summarization and triage workflows. We scoped a POC to run both hosted API and dedicated reserved capacity — compare throughput, latency, and most importantly quality. Today is mostly around the quality eval plan.
[01:12] Maya Ortiz: Correct. Our primary success criteria: accuracy of triage intent classification (we want >92% on our holdout), fidelity of clinical summarization (measured by ROUGE and human acceptability), and zero critical hallucinations on PHI-sensitive outputs. Also need strict format compliance for our downstream parser.
[01:40] Priya Nair: Great. We'll break that into quantitative checks and human-in-the-loop checks. Quantitative: classification accuracy, token-level edit distance (for format), and hallucination flags via QA heuristics. Human: spot checks for clinical correctness on a sample.

[02:10] Ravi Patel: For datasets, we can provide 1,200 de-identified triage notes plus 5k short chat transcripts. We want to make sure de-id is acceptable — there may be edge cases with initials.
[02:28] Priya Nair: That size is perfect for initial eval. We'll ask for a 1k golden set (labelled) and then a larger 5k stress set. Golden prompts — we need canonical prompts for each task (triage, summary, extraction). Please share current prompts or examples.

[03:05] Maya Ortiz: We have some prompts but they're ad-hoc. We want Redwood to propose standardized golden prompts we can A/B.
[03:12] Alex Chen: Yep, we'll provide a golden prompt library. Priya will propose 3-4 variants per task: conservative, balanced, and concise. We'll track which prompt achieves best tradeoffs.
[03:30] Priya Nair: On regression testing: we'll run current baseline model output (your internal baseline + an open checkpoint), then compare Redwood-hosted and Redwood-dedicated runs for any regression with a delta threshold. If quality drops >3% on key metrics, that's a regression trigger. We'll also capture format violations (e.g., missing JSON fields) as hard failures.
[04:00] Ravi Patel: How do you detect hallucinations? Sometimes models invent medications or dosages.
[04:08] Priya Nair: Good question — we use a mix of heuristic checks and model-based QA. Heuristics: named-entity cross-checks, units/dosage patterns, and a PHI presence detector. Model-based: we'll run a verification prompt that asks the model to assert confidence and cite input tokens; low confidence or unsupported claims get flagged. We'll include a sampling of flagged cases for human review.
[04:45] Sam Lee: On the infra side, if we run Redwood Dedicated we need to know footprint. What's typical for the 5k stress set?
[04:55] Priya Nair: For throughput baseline, it'll depend on model size; for a 13B dense model with quantization we expect ~120-200 requests/sec with batching tuned. For exact sizing we'll run a perf benchmark. For the POC we'll propose a dedicated pool with 2-4 GPUs for parallelism. We'll size after initial runs.

[05:30] Maya Ortiz: Timeline? We need a 3-week window to evaluate before presenting to the clinical board.
[05:38] Alex Chen: 3 weeks is doable. Proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) collect data + finalize prompts; week 1 run baseline and first Redwood-hosted benchmarks; week 2 run Redwood-dedicated + regression tests; week 3 human review and scoring and deliverable.
[06:00] Jordan: Procurement signoff will probably need an SOW and security addendum; can Redwood share SOC 2 and data residency docs?
[06:08] Alex Chen: Yes — we'll attach SOC 2, ISO notes, and KMS options; Priya will include notes about our private deployment options.
[06:20] Priya Nair: Note: if you need VPC/on-prem we have Redwood Private options; for the POC we usually keep data de-identified and use Hosted or Dedicated with encrypted-at-rest keys. We can support KMS/HSM integration if needed.

[06:50] Ravi Patel: Regarding scoring approach: we want a composite score that weights: triage accuracy (40%), summary quality (30%), hallucination rate penalties (20%), and format compliance (10%). Is that easy to compute?
[07:05] Priya Nair: Yes, that's straightforward. We'll compute per-sample metrics and aggregate weighted averages. For summary quality we'll combine ROUGE-L with a binary human acceptability flag. Hallucination rate is percent of flagged critical hallucinations; penalties applied as absolute point deductions.

[07:35] Maya Ortiz: For regression tests, can you produce a changelog-style report listing exact examples that regressed? We need diffs for clinical review.
[07:42] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll export per-example diffs and categorize by severity. We'll also attach the prompt version and model variant used.

[08:10] Ravi Patel: On golden prompts: make sure they include format templates (JSON schema) for the parser to consume. Even small whitespace or missing keys breaks our pipeline.
[08:22] Priya Nair: Understood. We'll codify the expected JSON schema and create prompts that explicitly instruct the model to output JSON with field types and examples. We'll treat missing/invalid JSON as a hard fail.

[09:00] Sam Lee: Any concerns about tokenization or strange truncation? We have long notes sometimes (2k tokens).
[09:07] Priya Nair: We'll set sequence length high for summarization runs; if model doesn't support long context we can chunk with overlap and stitch. We'll measure quality loss from chunking. Also we'll share quantization recommendations — e.g., int8 vs int4 tradeoffs — as part of the performance report.

[09:45] Alex Chen: Competitors question — do you evaluate against Anthropic or OpenAI baselines?
[09:50] Maya Ortiz: We want at least one external baseline for comparison.
[09:54] Priya Nair: We'll include an open checkpoint baseline and, if you approve, an OpenAI API run for apples-to-apples. Note that costs for third-party baselines will be billed or covered by PulseCare.

[10:20] Ravi Patel: How do we handle PII fallbacks? If a model hallucinates PHI, do you quarantine outputs?
[10:28] Priya Nair: Yes — flagged outputs will be quarantined in the eval pipeline and marked for human review. For Hosted we can attach data retention rules; for Dedicated/Private we can set shorter retention or disabled logging. We'll document in the security appendix.

[11:00] Maya Ortiz: Scoring thresholds — our board will need a pass/fail recommendation. Can you propose thresholds?
[11:07] Alex Chen: Based on your targets, we'll propose: triage accuracy >= 92% pass; summary acceptability >= 0.85 (human sample); critical hallucination rate < 0.5% pass; format compliance > 99% pass. We'll refine with you.

[12:00] Priya Nair: On eval harness: we'll provide a Dockerized runner that takes dataset CSV, runs prompts, computes metrics, and outputs per-sample JSON with metrics. Note CSV->JSON here may produce transcription errors in logs — sometimes headers misalign, so check carefully.

[12:30] Ravi Patel: For human review, how many samples?
[12:35] Priya Nair: We'll do a stratified sample of 200 examples for clinical review (balanced across urgent/non-urgent and long/short notes). That should give reasonable confidence intervals.

[13:05] Maya Ortiz: Do you support continuous regression after POC? We may want to track model drift.
[13:10] Alex Chen: Yes — Redwood Optimize can run periodic regression checks and alert on deviations. It's an add-on but we can include a trial.

[13:45] Sam Lee: Any known gotchas for JSON output validation? We've seen models output single quotes or trailing commas.
[13:50] Priya Nair: We'll run a post-processor that normalizes quotes and validates against JSON schema; if fixable by normalization we'll mark as soft failure; if structure is wrong we'll mark as hard fail. We'll log both raw and cleaned outputs for audit.

[14:20] Ravi Patel: Can you show a small example of golden prompts now?
[14:25] Priya Nair: Sure — quick example: 
Prompt (summarization): "You are a clinical summarizer. Input: <note>. Output JSON: {"summary": "<short summary>", "concise_reason": "<one-line reason>"}. Do not hallucinate facts not present in input. If unknown, say "UNKNOWN"."

[15:00] Maya Ortiz: Sounds good. We'll iterate.

[15:20] Alex Chen: OK let's recap next steps — Alex sends scope + pricing and security docs; Priya shares eval harness + golden prompt templates; PulseCare provides datasets and final success criteria; we schedule the first benchmark next week.
[15:40] Jordan: From procurement side, we'll need a short SOW and data addendum — send to jordan@pulsecare.io.
[15:48] Alex Chen: Will do. Anything else?
[15:52] Ravi Patel: One more ask — can you include the raw per-example diffs in a spreadsheet? Clinicians prefer row-level context.
[15:57] Priya Nair: Yes, we'll export diffs to CSV with columns: id, baseline_output, new_output, metric_delta, severity, notes.

[16:10] Alex Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and Slack with links.
[16:15] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript includes minor transcription artifacts (e.g., K V cache written as K V cache, some punctuation and speaker alignment may be off). References: Eval harness repo (link shared post-meeting), security docs (SOC2/ISO) and SOW template.
